observation: Original fixed land-first policy always played Otawara as a land on turn ≤10 when first seen and eligible, producing 0 held channel opportunities at turn 10 under that policy. This is not evidence the card fails as stax answer.
reserve_definition: Conditionally assume an already-resolved nonblue permanent stax threat is known and persists. If Otawara is in hand, never choose it for a land drop; play next best supported land instead if present, otherwise forfeit that turn's land drop. Do not give extra land plays, cards, mana or discounts. Keep existing fetch target and shock assumptions.
outputs: per-policy slot Warp held and land-payable as first spell
per-policy Otawara held and land-payable via 3U channel, hand only
per-policy forfeited land drop due to Otawara reservation
baseline and three Warp challenger variants all physical 100 cards
limitations: Two extreme fixed policies; an actual player may adapt dynamically and also preserve source development
Holding Otawara from turn one presumes preidentified permanent stax since turn one; never interpret as ordinary metagame probability
No real Rule of Law opponent chance, no extra ramp/card draw, no access to rule effects, actual game wins or all interaction
This corrects an experiment bias; original result remains recorded, not erased, and neither new policy certifies M6 or a deck swap
